title: Minimum Window Substring
statement:
A feed analytics job stores each user's activity as a string s, one character per event, in time order. Each character is an event type (for example v = view, c = click, s = share). Upper- and lowercase letters are different types.

A funnel report needs the shortest contiguous stretch of the log that contains every event in t, counting repeats: if t = "cca", the stretch must hold at least two c and at least one a. Order inside the stretch does not matter, and extra events are allowed.

Write def solution(s, t) that returns that stretch as a substring of s. If no stretch covers t, return "". If several stretches have the same shortest length, return the leftmost one (smallest start index).

examples.why: The LeetCode 76 example. "ADOBEC" also covers A, B, C but has length 6; "BANC" has length 4.
t needs two a events and the log has one, so no stretch works.
"ba" (start 1) and "ab" (start 4) both have length 2. Order inside does not matter, and the leftmost wins.

constraints: s and t contain only English letters; case matters

think.a: A window covers t when, for every character, the window has at least as many copies as t does. Order and extra characters do not matter. Return the substring itself, "" if none exists, and the smallest start index on a tie.

Grow the right end until the window first covers: "ADOBEC" (0..5). Shrink the left: dropping A breaks it. Grow again until another A arrives at index 10: "ADOBECODEBA", now shrink past A, D, O, B, E to "CODEBA". Grow to C at 12, shrink to "BANC". Best length goes 6, 6, 4.

think.q: What is the first idea that works?
think.a: For each start i, extend j until the window covers t, keeping a running count. That is O(n^2): 10^10 steps at the limit. Checking every substring from scratch would be O(n^3).

Variable-size sliding window (two pointers that only move right) with a count map of what is still needed. The key is one integer, missing, so checking "does the window cover t?" is O(1), not a loop over 52 letters.

1. need = Counter(t), missing = len(t), left = 0.
  2. For each right: if need[ch] > 0, decrement missing; always decrement need[ch].
  3. While missing == 0: record the window if strictly shorter, then give back s[left] (need += 1; if it goes above 0, missing += 1) and move left.
  4. Return the best slice or "".

t longer than s. Repeats in t ("aa" needs two). Case ("A" is not "a"). The answer is the whole string. The answer sits at the very end. Ties between equal-length windows. Characters in s that are not in t (their count goes negative, which is fine).

hints: Keep two indices, left and right, that only move forward. Grow right until the window covers t, then shrink left as far as it stays valid.
Store need = Counter(t) and decrement it as characters enter. Track missing, the number of required characters still owed, so the "is it valid?" check is just missing == 0.

When a character leaves on the left, add it back to need. Only if its count becomes positive did you lose a required copy, so only then missing += 1. Record the window before you shrink it, and use < so the first shortest window stays.
solution:
from collections import Counter

def solution(s, t):
    need = Counter(t)        # how many of each type the window still owes (negative = surplus)
    missing = len(t)         # total events still owed; 0 means the window covers t
    best_start = 0
    best_len = len(s) + 1    # longer than any real window, so "none found yet"
    left = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        if need[ch] > 0:     # this event pays off something t still needs
            missing -= 1
        need[ch] -= 1
        while missing == 0:  # valid window: record it, then shrink from the left
            if right - left + 1 < best_len:   # strict: keep the leftmost on ties
                best_start = left
                best_len = right - left + 1
            drop = s[left]
            need[drop] += 1
            if need[drop] > 0:                # we just gave up a required event
                missing += 1
            left += 1
    if best_len > len(s):
        return ""
    return s[best_start:best_start + best_len]
explain:
Example 3, s = "xbaxab", t = "ab", missing = 2:

  • right 0 x: not needed, need[x] = -1.
  • right 1 b: needed, missing = 1.
  • right 2 a: needed, missing = 0. Window 0..2 "xba", best = 3. Drop x: need[x] back to 0, still valid. Window 1..2 "ba", best = 2. Drop b: need[b] = 1, missing = 1, left = 3.
  • right 3 x, right 4 a: need[a] goes to -1 (a surplus), nothing owed changes.
  • right 5 b: missing = 0. Window 3..5 length 3, not better. Shrink to 4..5 "ab": length 2, not strictly shorter, so "ba" stays.

Each index enters the window once and leaves at most once, so the total work is O(n + m) even though there is a while inside the for. Storing a start and a length instead of slicing every candidate keeps each record O(1).
complexity: O(n + m) time, O(k) extra space for the counts (k = distinct letters, at most 52)

talk: O(n + m) time: right moves n times and left moves at most n times in total, so the inner while is amortised O(1).
One Counter does double duty: positive means still needed, negative means surplus. missing is the sum of the positive parts, so validity is missing == 0 instead of comparing two dicts each step.
I store best_start and best_len and slice once at the end. Slicing every candidate would copy up to n characters each time.
Tie-break: I record before shrinking and only replace on a strictly shorter window, so the first (leftmost) shortest window wins.
Edge cases: repeats in t, case-sensitive letters, t longer than s (return ""), and the answer being the whole log.
extensions: Order matters now: the stretch must contain t as a subsequence (LC 727). Why does the count map no longer work, and what replaces it?
Return the length only, but s is a stream of events too large to keep: what do you need to store, and when can you drop old events?
Each event also has a timestamp: find the shortest time span that covers t instead of the fewest events.
Return all shortest windows, not just the leftmost. What changes in the comparison?
Fixed-size version: does any window of exactly len(t) events match t as a multiset (LC 567)?
